contract: Compare complete UTF-8 conversions for every single byte, every byte pair in the multibyte profiles, and seeded streams. The ASS decoder exposes the visible string. Public glibc iconv supplies complete bytes after NUL and the first refused sequence's byte offset; the worker checks the visible prefix against ASS when present.
The exact differential byte and pair results in reviewed-mappings.tsv identify the strict-profile mapping exceptions observed on AArch64. Every compared matrix is retained with its reference fold.

open_deviations.reading: An unmapped CP949 pair is refused at the start of the pair
open_deviations.clause: POSIX iconv(): on an invalid input sequence the input position points to the beginning of that sequence; Microsoft CP949.TXT 2.01 has no A2E8.

open_policies.policy: The strict big5 profile decodes Big5 as the Encoding Standard does
open_policies.undecided: WHATWG Encoding Standard, Big5 decoder and index-big5: lead bytes 81 to FE, the Hong Kong supplement with its plane 2 characters, the codes 8862, 8864, 88A3 and 88A5 as two code points each, and no single byte beyond ASCII.
open_policies.rule: Refuses byte 80; maps 8740 to U+43F0, 8862 to U+00CA U+0304, C6A1 to U+2460 and F9FE to U+FFED.
open_policies.reference_rule: glibc 2.39 iconv decodes 80 as U+0080, refuses 8740 and 8862, and maps C6A1 to U+F6B1 and F9FE to U+2593.
open_policies.compat: triergon_subtitles::compat::charset::receiver_charset, whose gbk, big5, shift_jis, cp950 and euc-kr profiles convert as the reference build's glibc iconv does

open_policies.policy: The strict gbk profile decodes GBK as the Encoding Standard does
open_policies.undecided: WHATWG Encoding Standard, gb18030 decoder (the GBK decoder) with index-gb18030 and index-gb18030-ranges: lead bytes 81 to FE, trail bytes 40 to 7E and 80 to FE, the two-byte codes GB18030 adds to CP936 (the user-defined areas AAA1 to AFFE, F8A1 to FEFE and A140 to A7A0 among them), 80 as U+20AC, and four-byte codes.
open_policies.rule: Decodes the 2,149 two-byte codes GB18030 adds to CP936: A140 as U+E4C6, AAA1 as U+E000, A2E3 as U+20AC, A6D9 as U+FE10.
open_policies.reference_rule: glibc 2.39 iconv refuses them at the start of the pair.
open_policies.compat: triergon_subtitles::compat::charset::receiver_charset, whose gbk, big5, shift_jis, cp950 and euc-kr profiles convert as the reference build's glibc iconv does

open_policies.policy: The strict shift_jis profile decodes Shift_JIS as the Encoding Standard does
open_policies.undecided: WHATWG Encoding Standard, Shift_JIS decoder and index-jis0208: ASCII as itself, 80 as U+0080, A1 to DF as the halfwidth katakana, lead bytes 81 to 9F and E0 to FC with the NEC and IBM extensions, and F040 to F9FC as U+E000 to U+E757.
open_policies.rule: Decodes 5C as U+005C, 7E as U+007E and 80 as U+0080; maps 8160 to U+FF5E, 8161 to U+2225, 817C to U+FF0D, 8191 to U+FFE0, 8192 to U+FFE1 and 81CA to U+FFE2; decodes the lead bytes F0 to FC and the extension rows (8740 as U+2460).
open_policies.reference_rule: glibc 2.39 iconv decodes 5C as U+00A5 and 7E as U+203E, refuses 80, maps 8160 to U+301C, 8161 to U+2016, 817C to U+2212, 8191 to U+00A2, 8192 to U+00A3 and 81CA to U+00AC, and refuses the extension rows.
open_policies.compat: triergon_subtitles::compat::charset::receiver_charset, whose gbk, big5, shift_jis, cp950 and euc-kr profiles convert as the reference build's glibc iconv does

open_policies.policy: The strict windows-950 profile converts code page 950 as Windows does
open_policies.undecided: Microsoft CP950.TXT 2.01 lists the code page's assigned characters; Windows converts the four user-defined areas FA40 to FEFE, 8E40 to A0FE, 8140 to 8DFE and C6A1 to C8FE to U+E000 to U+F848, and the single bytes 80 and FF to U+0080 and U+F8F8.
open_policies.rule: Maps FF to U+F8F8 and every user-defined pair to private use, FA40 to U+E000.
open_policies.reference_rule: glibc 2.39 iconv converts CP950 as BIG5: of the user-defined areas it maps C6A1 to C8FE only, and it refuses FF and pairs such as FA40.
open_policies.compat: triergon_subtitles::compat::charset::receiver_charset, whose gbk, big5, shift_jis, cp950 and euc-kr profiles convert as the reference build's glibc iconv does

open_policies.policy: The strict euc-kr profile decodes EUC-KR as the Encoding Standard does: the UHC pairs, and no byte 80 to 9F
open_policies.undecided: WHATWG Encoding Standard, EUC-KR decoder and index-euc-kr: lead bytes 81 to FE, trail bytes 41 to FE, the UHC extension pairs of code page 949, and no single byte beyond ASCII; ISO/IEC 2022 and ISO/IEC 4873 let an EUC carry C1 controls in 80 to 9F, which glibc decodes.
open_policies.rule: Refuses every byte 80 to 9F, alone or in a pair; decodes the UHC pairs (8141 as U+AC02) and refuses A2E8, as index-euc-kr and code page 949 do.
open_policies.reference_rule: glibc 2.39 iconv decodes 80 to 9F as the C1 controls U+0080 to U+009F (8141 as U+0081 U+0041), refuses the UHC pairs with a lead byte from A1 on, and maps A2E8 to U+327E.
open_policies.compat: triergon_subtitles::compat::charset::receiver_charset, whose gbk, big5, shift_jis, cp950 and euc-kr profiles convert as the reference build's glibc iconv does
